$comment: Exit codes of every hem-tool command (REQ-TOOL-003 … 028). Taken from the C implementation at encedo-hem-c-api 1.2.0: the per-command enumerations in its headers and the registry's help texts. The `common` codes apply to every command; a command lists only its own additional codes. Scripts rely on these numbers.

common.1: failure — the message says which (device, cloud or login error)
common.2: usage error — bad arguments, missing passphrase or environment
common.12: the SDK could not be initialised: its crypto library is missing or not the one it was built against (REQ-TOOL-024); printed before any command runs
common.13: --mobile: the push was not answered in time
common.14: --mobile: the push was rejected on the phone

cert-install.3: no certificate chain delivered and no current serial to compare
cert-install.5: the harvested chain would not parse
cert-install.9: the device never returned after the reboot

tls-recover.3: the provisioning cloud delivered no usable bundle
tls-recover.4: the device did not return serving HTTPS

recovery.3: expired certificate and the cloud delivered no renewal (one attempt per run)
recovery.4: neither https nor http answers, or a bounded wait ran out
recovery.5: a TLS failure that is not an expired certificate (hostname, CA)

keys pub.$comment: symmetric keys have no public material and still exit 0

keys types.2: unknown TYPE (the valid names are printed)

random.1: also: the transient key could not be removed afterwards

selftest.3: the battery ran but the device reports a fault (fls_state != 0)

ext pair.3: the QR was not scanned in time
ext pair.4: the device refused the pairing (406: slots full / already paired)

ext login.3: the push was not answered in time

init-device.4: the RTC is still unset after the check-in (403)
init-device.5: the configuration was rejected by the device (400)

init-wizard.4: the RTC is still unset after the check-in (403)
init-wizard.5: the configuration was rejected by the device (400)
init-wizard.6: cancelled by the operator (end of input, or declined at the summary)

wipe-device.3: declined — the typed hostname did not confirm
wipe-device.4: --wait: the device did not answer again after the wipe
